about: Reply-door, caller-signal, redaction and compile-lint rules as data. The TypeScript door (product/shared/safety/index.ts) and the Python door (product/voice) load this one file and are held to cases.json. Rules are evaluated in array order; the first reply rule that fires decides. Industry-neutral rules have scope.packs absent; sector rules name their pack.

regex.dialect: Common subset of ECMAScript (flags 'iu') and Python re (flags re.I). No named groups, no \p{...}, no variable-width lookbehind. \b is used only next to Latin letters. Patterns run on the NORMALISED text.
normalise: See normalisation (the executable contract). PATTERNS get only the Devanagari part (NFC, nukta dropped, chandrabindu -> anusvara) before compiling; they are not lowercased.
regex.clause_scope: none patterns shield the whole sentence (warnings, factual frames). noneClause patterns (negations) shield only the clause holding a match of the anchor pattern (all[anchor], default the last all group; for any-rules each any pattern). Clauses are cut by regex.clause_split; a preceding segment shorter than 12 characters joins the clause after it. coClause: every all-group must match inside the anchor's clause; if that clause holds a back-reference (regex.back_reference), the previous clause joins it.

redact.about: Redaction is context-first (red team: a checksum gate lowers recall on ASR output, because a misheard digit fails the checksum and the number leaks). Context near a digit run masks it; with no context, a checksum (Luhn for 13-19 digits, Verhoeff for 12) raises confidence enough to mask. 10-digit Indian phone numbers are not masked unless an OTP/PIN context sits next to them.

T-L3.about: Drops facts whose purpose tag is not allowed for the call category, and facts tagged service/logistics/identity whose text reads as an offer on a service or transactional call (a mis-tag).

T-L4.about: Refuse any link or bare domain in the config (outside brand.verifiedDomains itself) whose host is not a verified domain or its subdomain. Email addresses are not links. Link shorteners are never verified.

links.about: A host is accepted when it equals a verified domain or ends with '.' + a verified domain. Spoken forms ('dot com') are rewritten to '.com' before matching.

normalisation.about: The one normalisation both doors apply, in this order, to every text before matching (M2: TS and Python must agree). Ranges are inclusive hex code points.
steps: form: Unicode normalisation form (NFKC folds fullwidth and compatibility forms, e.g. U+017F long s -> s)
strip: delete these code points (invisible formatting: soft hyphen, zero-width, joiners, bidi marks)
fold: replace each key character with its value (Cyrillic/Greek homoglyphs, curly quotes, chandrabindu -> anusvara)
drop: delete these code points (Devanagari nukta)
space: every code point in these ranges becomes U+0020; runs of spaces collapse to one; trim

words_to_amounts.about: Spoken amounts (M1): a run of number words followed by a multiplier becomes digits before amount parsing, e.g. 'paanch hazaar' -> 5000, 'do lakh pachaas hazaar' -> 250000. Number words alone (no multiplier) are not amounts. Keys are post-normalisation.
